solution:
The correct answer is "No error." [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence appears to be grammatically correct and does not contain any errors.
 
• It is a conditional sentence expressing **a hypothetical situation.**
 
• **"If I were your mother" **this segment uses the correct form of the verb for unreal, hypothetical situations or conditions.
 
• The construction** "would have" + past participle (taken)** is typical for these kind of unreal conditionals.
 
• **"of you and your sisters" **correctly completes the phrase** "taken care of"** which is a common idiom meaning **to look after or be responsible for someone.**

So, the correct answer is Option 3. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

• "If I were your mother, I **would take** care of you and your sisters."
 
 
• This sentence is an example of a **"second conditional"** sentence. It implies **an unreal or hypothetical **situation in the present or future. The speaker is imagining what she would do right now or in the future if she were their mother.
 
 
 
• Both sentences are grammatically correct. The one to use would depend if you're talking about a hypothetical past (with 'would have taken') or a hypothetical present or future (with 'would take').

subject: ENG
question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

Her health has being / steadily improving / since she started / practising yoga.
solution:
The erroneous part is '**Her health has being'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 The words ‘**being**’ and ‘**been**’ are sometimes confused, the word ‘**been**’ is always used after ‘**have**’ whereas ‘**being**’ is never used after ‘have’. It is used after ‘**be**’.
 
 
• 
 '**Been**' is the past participle of the verb '**be**' and is usually used with the perfect aspect with ‘**have**’ in all its forms i.e.** had and has**

 
 
• 
 **Ex**: I have *been *busy. 
 
 
 
 
• 
 '**being**' is the present participle of the verb '**be**' and can be used with the continuous form of the verb '**be**' is all its forms i.e. *am, is, was, are and were.*

 
 
• 
 **Ex**: When I arrived at the scene of the accident the victim was **being **placed in an ambulance.
 
 
• 
 I don't know why but John is **being **really difficult today.
 
 
 
 
• 
 Hence, the correct answer is** option 4.**
 

**The correct sentence**: *Her health has **been **steadily improving since she started practising yoga.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__**Being as a noun**__

__
 
• The word '**being**' can also be used as a noun.

 
 
• **Ex**: A human being.
 
 

**Being as a gerund**__

 
• The word '**being**' can be used as a gerund which is a type of noun.

 
 
• **Ex**: Do all actors like being famous?
 
• His being clumsy caused the accident.

• **Conditional Sentences** (Type I) refer to the **future**.
 
• Action in the future will only happen if a certain condition is fulfilled by that time.
 
• ​We don't know for sure whether the condition actually will be fulfilled or not, but the conditions seem rather realistic – so we think it is likely to happen.
 
 
• **Example**:** *****If **I find her address, **I’ll send **her an invitation.*
 
 
• I want to send an invitation to a friend. I just have to find her address. I am quite sure, however, that I will find it.
 
 
 
• **Example**:* **If **John has the money, he **will buy **a Ferrari.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is about sloths, a species of mammals known for their slow movement and their tree-dwelling lifestyle in the south and central American rain forests.
 
• The best word to describe inhabitants native to a particular place is "natives". Hence "natives" is the appropriate choice for the first blank, which refers to the sloths' natural habitat.
 
• In the second blank, we need a phrase that implies leisure, relax or free time, suggesting the sloth's slow, leisurely pace of life. The term "vacation" fits this context ideally as it conveys a sense of extended rest or leisure time.
 
• The use of these terms, "natives" and "vacation", completes the sentence forming a metaphorical but accurate depiction of the sloth's characteristic lifestyle.
 
• The options "resident", "habitant", "locals", and "quit" or "rest" or "recess" don't provide the same level of symbolic imagery, making them less suitable than "natives" and "vacation".

Therefore, the correct answer is- 'Option 4'.

**Given below are six sentences A-F, of which A and F are static and B-E have been jumbled. Pick the option that gives the correct order of the jumbled sentences.**

A. Suddenly I noticed smoke pouring in through the seams of the ceiling.

B. Groping our way to the front door we all ran out into the front yard.

C. The smoke began to fill the room so quickly that we could barely see.

D. I ran to the neighbours to call the fire department.

E. By the time we made our way outside, the whole roof was engulfed in flames.

F. I saw mother run back into the house and I screamed, “Mom! No!”
solution:
The correct answer is** 'ACBEDF'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting off a story, starting of an incident or an event, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
• In the given question, sentence A is the first sentence. And sentence F is the last one.
 
• We have to rearrange the rest of the sentences accordingly.
 
• Sentence A is *'Suddenly I noticed smoke pouring in through the seams of the ceiling.'* this is the starting of an incident.
 
• **Sentence A** tells us that the author noticed the smoke coming from the ceiling. After it, **Sentence C** should be used because it expresses** 'how smoke'** began to fill the room.
 
• After seeing the smoke in the room, the author ran out of the room to the front yard. Hence, **Sentence B **should be the next one.
 
• **Sentence E** should be the next one because it tells us how the roof got engulfed in flames as soon as they ran out into the front yard.
 
• Next, **Sentence D** should be used next because **Sentence D** tells us about what the author did after reaching the front yard i.e. he ran to the neighbours to call the fire department.
 
• Thus the sequence becomes:
 
 
• A: Suddenly I noticed smoke pouring in through the seams of the ceiling.
 
• C: The smoke began to fill the room so quickly that we could barely see.
 
• B: Groping our way to the front door we all ran out into the front yard.
 
• E: By the time we made our way outside, the whole roof was engulfed in flames.
 
• D: I ran to the neighbours to call the fire department.
 
• F: I saw mother run back into the house and I screamed, “Mom! No!”
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 2.

 ​

Correct Sequence:__ *Suddenly I noticed smoke pouring in through the seams of the ceiling. The smoke began to fill the room so quickly that we could barely see. Groping our way to the front door we all ran out into the front yard. By the time we made our way outside, the whole roof was engulfed in flames. I ran to the neighbours to call the fire department. I saw mother run back into the house and I screamed, “Mom! No!”*

subject: ENG
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.**

“Where is your office?” Anita said to me.

options.text: Anita asked where my office were.
Anita enquired where my office was.
Anita asked where was my office?

solution:
The correct answer is: "**Anita enquired where my office was.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Reported speech is used to convey what someone said in the past.
 
• In reported speech, the tense of the verb often changes from the original sentence.
 
• When reporting a question, we use an introductory verb like "**asked**" or "**enquired**" and change the word order of the sentence.
 
• To convert the direct speech "Where is your office?" into reported speech:
 
 
• Change the reporting verb (**said**) to an appropriate verb like "**enquired**" for a question.
 
• Move the reporting verb to the past tense ("enquired").
 
• Introduce a reporting clause ("**where**") to report the question.
 
• Change the pronoun "**your**" to match the context of the reporting clause ("**my**").
 
• Change the word order to place the subject ("**my office**") before the verb ("**was**").
 
 
 
• The reported speech version is: "*Anita enquired where my office was.*"

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

You said, “ Priya kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.”

options.text: You said that Priya kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.
You said that Priya had kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.
You said that Priya kept watching television till her mother had exploded at her.
You said that Priya had kept watching television till her mother had exploded at her.

solution:
The correct option is: **1) You said that Priya kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence involves a **time clause** ("till her mother exploded at her"), which is used to describe when the action of "watching television" ended.
 
• The use of the word **"till"** indicates a specific point in time when the action of watching television stopped, making it a time clause. 
 
• In indirect speech, when the reporting verb is in the past tense (like "said"), the action in the direct speech is generally shifted to the past tense.
 
• In this case, since the action of watching television is continuous up until a specific point in time (when the mother exploded), the past simple tense "kept" remains appropriate, and the time clause "till her mother exploded" is in the past simple as well.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***You said that Priya kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.***

question:
**Choose the option that is the indirect form of the sentence.**

Vandana said, “I’m being dropped to office today’’.

options.text: Vandana said that she should be dropped to office today.
Vandana said that I am being dropped to office on that day.
Vandana said that she was being dropped to office that day.
Vandana said she was dropped to office today.

solution:
Here the correct answer is **Vandana said that she was being dropped to office that day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:- 

__
 
• In the indirect form,** 'today'** changes to **'that day'**. So, we can reject option 1 and 4.
 
• The first person pronoun i.e **'I' **changes to third person i.e. **'she'**.
 
• The direct form is in **present continuous form** as indicated by **(being dropped)**. So, the indirect form will be in **past continuous form (was being dropped)**.
 
• The only option which shows the structure of **past continuous** form is **Option 3**.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

*Therefore, the correct indirect form of the given direct form is* *Vandana said that she was being dropped to office that day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• *When we convert a sentence from* *direct to indirect speech*, we make the following changes:-

 
 
• Quotation marks are omitted and the sentence ends with a full stop. 
 
• The tense of the verb, in the reported speech involving any order, request and instruction does not undergo any change during the conversion from direct to indirect mode.
 
• This is also true if the statement is a universal truth. 
 
• If the reporting verb is in the present tense, it does not undergo any change.
 
• We add the word 'to' before the verb if the verb is in bare infinitive.
 
• When the reporting or principal verb is in the present tense, all present tenses of the direct are changed into the corresponding past tenses.
 
• Words expressing nearness in time or place are generally converted into into words expressing distance.
 
 
• For Example - Now becomes then, today becomes that day, yesterday becomes the previous day, this becomes that etc.
 
 
 
• In reporting commands and requests, the verb expressing command or request is added and the imperative is changed into the infinitive. 
 
• In reporting questions the verbs like asked, inquired are added 
 
• In reporting exclamations and wishes, the verbs expressing exclamation or wish are added. 
 
• When we convert a sentence from the direct to the indirect mode(especially for a sentence ending with a mark of interrogation), we reverse the subject-verb placement. In direct sentences, we have the verb before the subject; while in indirect, the verb follows the subject.

***__Key Points__**

To change the sentence to a direct speech we need to follow the following steps:

__
 
• In the reporting speech, the **verb ***told *will change to *said/says*.

• The verb ***Would ***will change ***will***.
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• Indirect: *She told her that she would perform a dance.*
 
• Direct: *She said to her, “I will perform a dance.”*
 
 
 
 
 
• The conjunction '*that*' should be replaced by an inverted comma, enclosing the reported speech.
 
• The possessive adjective their ***will change to *our*.
 
• The pronoun *they *will change to *we*.

Here are some rules that should be followed while converting an indirect speech to direct speech:

 
• Use the reporting verb such as (*say, said to*) in its correct tense.
 
• Put a comma before the statement and the first letter of the statement should be in capital letter.
 
• Insert *question marks*, *quotation marks*, *exclamation marks *and *full stop*, based on the mood of the sentence. And remove the infinitive words like request, ask, order wherever necessary.
 
• Remove the conjunctions like (*that, if *or *whether*) wherever necessary.
 
• Where the reporting verb is in the past tense in indirect, change it to present tense in the direct speech.
 
• Change the past perfect tense either into present perfect tense or past indefinite tense, as necessary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of a **tag question**, which is used to confirm or seek agreement about the information stated.
 
• In a tag question, the auxiliary verb and subject pronoun in the tag must match the main verb and subject in the main clause.
 
• The main clause says, "You have a lot of coconut trees in your village," which is a positive statement. The tag must therefore be negative.
 
• The correct negative tag for "You have" is **"don’t you?"**, as it follows the rule of using the opposite polarity (positive statement + negative tag).

• **Tag Question Rules:**

 
 
• If the main sentence is positive, the tag question must be negative. Example: "He is coming, isn’t he?"
 
• If the main sentence is negative, the tag question must be positive. Example: "She doesn’t like coffee, does she?"
 
• The auxiliary verb in the tag must match the verb used in the main sentence. If no auxiliary is present, use "do/does/did" as appropriate.
 
 
 
• **Common Errors in Tag Questions:**
 
 
• Using the wrong polarity (e.g., positive tag with a positive statement).
 
• Mismatching the subject or auxiliary verb in the tag.

• The subject of the sentence is "none," which is a **singular noun**. The verb should agree with the singular subject, so "knows" is the correct verb form.

 **None **is a singular indefinite pronoun that can mean no one or not any.

In this sentence, **none **means **no one**, and it is the subject of the verb knows. The phrase **than you **is not the subject, but a complement that shows the comparison.

 
 
• 
 
Therefore, the verb **knows **agrees with the singular subject **none**, not the second person pronoun **you**.

 
 
• 
 
For example, you can say:**None of us knows the answer. **(**None **is the subject and **knows **is the verb. **Of us** is a prepositional phrase that modifies none.)

• Here, in the sentence, we need to use the past tense of the verb(**did**) because the sentence refers to the present moment.

Our microwave oven is out of order and __repairing is needed for it.__
solution:
The correct answer is- 'needs to be repaired.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the *conjunction *'**and**' joins two clauses of the **same degree **and **importance**.
 
• As the first clause is in **present indefinite tense **so the second sentence should **also **be in **present indefinite tense**.
 
• For a **singular subject **(*microwave oven*) a **singular verb **(*needs*) should be used.
 
• Thus ***option 3 ***is the correct answer.

**And the correct sentence is: ***Our microwave oven is out of order and **needs to be repaired **for it*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Let's learn the use of various conjunctions:

 
 
• Coordinating Conjunctions: They join like with like. In other words, they join a noun with another noun or an adjective with another adjective. There are seven in total: *for, and, nor, but, or, yet, *and *so*.

 
 
• Example: *He was late for school, so he took a shortcut.*
 
 
 
• Subordinating Conjunctions: They join *subordinate clauses *to *main clauses*. Common examples are *although, because, if, since, unless, until,* and *while*.
 
 
• Example: *Because it was raining (main clause), we had to cancel the class picnic (subordinate clause).*
 
 
 
• Correlative Conjunctions: They are used in pairs to join alternatives or equal elements. The most common pairs are *either...or, neither...nor, *and *not only...but also.*
 
 
• *​*Example: *You can have either chocolate or vanilla ice cream.*

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the action **started **in the morning and it is **still **going on.
 
• So the sentence is in the **present perfect continuous tense**.
 
• We know that the structure of the *present perfect continuous *tense is:
 
 
• *subject + has/have + been + verb + ing + since/for + object.*
 
 
• Example: He has been playing in the garden for 2 hours.*
 
 
 
 
 
• Thus *option 3 *is the correct answer.

And the correct sentence is: *Since 10 o’clock in the morning, **he has been working **on this design.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__** 

 
• We can use **present perfect continuous **tense for:

 
 
• to talk about a **finished activity **in the **recent past**. Using the present perfect continuous focuses on the activity.

 
 
• Example: *I’ve just been cleaning the car. *(The car is wet and clean.)
 
 
 
• for a single activity that **began **at a point in the **past **and is **still continuing**:
 
 
• Example: *He’s been living in the village since 1995. *(He is still living in the village.)
 
 
 
• to talk about repeated activities that started at a particular time in the **past **and are **still continuing **up until now:

question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

__To keeping__ the photo in front of her, Jia drew the picture.
solution:
The correct answer is '**Keeping**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given above sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• In the above-given sentence, '**To keeping**' will be replaced by ‘Keeping’.
 
• As per the general rule, "**keeping**" is used **as a gerund** which makes "**keeping warm**" **a noun phrase**.
 
• "**to keep**" is the **infinitive form**, wherein "**to**" is simply **part of the infinitive**. So, one might say that "**to keep warm**" is a **sentence adverb**.
 
• **both are correct**, but **they differ grammatically**.
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• ***Keeping/to keep **her voice conversational, she asked him without looking up. (correct)*
 
• ***To keeping** her voice conversational, she asked him without looking up. (incorrect)*
 
 
 
• ​Here in the given above sentence, '**To keeping**' is used**, **which is wrong according to the rule.
 
• According to the explanation and example that are given above, ‘Keeping’ is the most appropriate substitute to the underlined segment.

**Correct sentence:** *Keeping the photo in front of her, Jia drew the picture.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• **"Being kept":** This use of passive voice makes it unclear who is keeping the photo in front of Jia.

 
 
• Is someone else placing it there for her?
 
• Passive voice is not appropriate in this context, because it shifts the focus away from what Jia is doing.
 
• This form would suggest that the photo somehow remained in front of Jia as she drew, but does not indicate that she herself placed or kept it there.
 
 
 
• **"To have kept"**: Using "to have" followed by the past participle of a verb is used to form the perfect infinitive.
 
 
• In this context, it would suggest that the action of Jia keeping the photo in front of her occurred (and finished) before she drew the picture.
 
• It is not the right tense in this context.

• Sentence B introduces a negative consequent i.e., a decrease in attention span due to the adoption of e-learning. Therefore, it follows C logically.

P. An extensive body of research demonstrates the business benefits of flexible working.

Q. Flexible work is still regarded as an add-on, something we do for mothers for a few months when they are back from parental leave.

R. Yet despite this overwhelming evidence, access to flexible work and careers is not widespread.

S. But in the face of rapid changes to the way we work, organisations need to move beyond just having policies for flexible working or making ad-hoc adjustments for certain individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Sentence P offers a strong start by introducing a general statement regarding the business benefits of flexible working, based on extensive research.
 
• R expands on this point by addressing a contradiction, which is the lack of widespread access to flexible work, despite the presented evidence.
 
• Q then furthers the argument by providing a reason for this contradiction - flexible work is generally viewed as a temporary solution for mothers returning from parental leave.
 
• Finally, S provides a logical conclusion, suggesting that organizations should move beyond ad-hoc solutions and policies, and adopt flexible working strategies due to the rapid changes in the way we work.

**Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.**

• **F**: He worked his fingers to the bone, but it seemed that no one cared.

solution:
The correct answer is- '**CADB**.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• By reading the above-given options we can understand that the subject of the passage is **a child**.
 
• **C **will come **first **as it introduces the **subject **(*The child*) of the passage.
 
• **A **will follow **next **as the **pronoun **(*they*) refers to the **noun **(*parents*).
 
• **D **will follow **B **as the **adverb **(*there*) is pointing towards the **noun **(*the side*) mentioned in part **B**.
 
• Thus *option 2 *is the correct answer.

The correct sequence is:

**C**. The child turned to look at her parents.

**A**. They were not there ahead of him.

**B**. He turned to look on the side.

**D**. They were not there either. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• Here are some tips to solve the para jumbles:
 
 
• You need to understand the idea behind the paragraph. If you can understand the idea/theme of the paragraph it is easy to put the sentences in order then.
 
• You should look out for the starting or the concluding sentences in the question. Sometimes they are clearly visible and can help you immensely in identifying the correct sequence.
 
• You need to know the relationships between different sentences to put them in the right sequence. 
 
• You should first fix the relationships of sentences, put them in order and then check the options.
 
• Transition words and contrasting words also help in finding clean relationships between sentences of the sentence rearrangement.
 
• Do not over depend on options, they only confuse you if you keep looking at them, use them as facilitators only, especially to fix your first sentence.
 
• The whole paragraph should have a coherent idea and flow when arranged in the correct order.

subject: ENG
question: Which of these ceremonies takes place while the sovereign is seated on the coronation chair?
solution:
The correct answer is** "the anointing, the investiture".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The anointing: According to the passage, the anointing ceremony takes place when the King's ceremonial robe is removed and he sits in the Coronation Chair. This is when the Archbishop of Canterbury anoints the King's hands, chest, and head with holy oil made from a secret blend of ingredients. 
 
• The investiture: After the anointing ceremony, the investiture takes place when the sovereign is still seated on the Coronation Chair. The sovereign is then presented with the regalia, including the Royal Orb, the Sceptre, and the Sovereign's Sceptre, before the Archbishop places St Edward's Crown on the King's head.
 
• The recognition and oath: The recognition and the oath are two ceremonies that take place while the king is standing next to the Coronation Chair, not while he is seated on it.
 
• The enthronement does not take place while the sovereign is seated on the Coronation Chair. Instead, this happens after the investiture when the King leaves the Coronation Chair and moves to the throne.

**Hence, the correct answer is 'Option 2'**

question: The passage is mainly about

options.text: the ancient documentation of Roman history
the ancient Roman and Greek histories
the use of myths and folklore in ancient Roman history

The correct answer is** 'the ancient documentation of Roman history'.**

__
 
• The passage discusses the lack of early written records for the regal period and early republic of Roman history.
 
• It explains the onset of historical writing in Rome, starting with Greek historians and Rome’s first native historian, Quintus Fabius Pictor.
 
• The passage elaborates on how the Roman annalistic tradition developed, entailing year-by-year accounts of Roman history by various historians.
 
• It touches on the difficulties faced by ancient historians in accurately documenting early Roman history due to the reliance on limited sources such as lists of annual magistrates, religious records, and laws.
 
• The pointing out of historical embellishments and inaccuracies due to the use of Roman and Greek folklore also underscores the challenges in documenting authentic early Roman history.
 
• The focus is on the broader theme of how early events in Roman history were documented rather than on specific details about the use of myths or Fabius Pictor alone.

subject: ENG
question: Which period in ancient Roman history is most poorly documented?
solution:
The correct answer is** '509–280 BC'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explicitly states that "The regal period (753–509 BC) and the early republic (509–280 BC) are the most poorly documented periods of Roman history."
 
• It explains that historical accounts of Rome were not written until much later, long after these periods had passed.
 
• This lack of contemporary documentation means that there is much less reliable information available about this time in Roman history.
 
• Ancient historians, such as Quintus Fabius Pictor, who wrote during the Second Punic War, began documenting Roman history well after the early republic period.
 
• Additionally, the passage describes the challenges faced by ancient historians in reconstructing events from these early periods, indicating the scarcity of accurate records.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: '27 BC- AD 14' corresponds to the reign of Augustus, for which many historical accounts exist.
 
• Option 2: '218 BC to 167 BC' is covered by some of Livy's extant books and therefore better documented.
 
• Option 3: '218–201 BC' is the period of the Second Punic War, which is well-documented, especially by historians like Fabius Pictor.

In the given sentence the underlined word may have been incorrectly spelt. Identify the option that rectifies the spelling. If there is no error in spelling, select ‘No error’.

The British Government claimed that the Jalianwala Bagh massacre was an __inadvertant__ measure taken by the police.
solution:
The correct answer is **"inadvertent".**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The underlined word in the sentence is **"inadvertant."** This word is **incorrectly spelled. **The correct spelling is **"inadvertent."**
 
• The term **"inadvertent" **is derived from the Latin word **"advertentem," **meaning **"to pay attention to" or "to notice." **When combined with the prefix **"in-,"** it gains the **opposite meaning. **
 
• Thus, **"inadvertent" **refers to **an action or result that wasn't intended or planned; it happened by accident.**
 
• The sentence **"The British Government claimed that the Jalianwala Bagh massacre was an inadvertant measure taken by the police" **uses this term to say the massacre was an unintended consequence of police action, according to the British Government.
 
• However, the word **"inadvertant" **is **mis-spelled. **There is a clear error in the sentence, so option 2, "No error," is incorrect.
 
• Neither** option 3 ("inedvartent") **nor **4 ("inadvartent")** correctly spell the word in question. They are merely other possible misspellings and do not provide the solution to this question.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** option 1 ("inadvertent").**
 
• Applying this, the sentence would read:** "The British Government claimed that the Jalianwala Bagh massacre was an inadvertent measure taken by the police,"** which is grammatically correct and semantically accurate.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Option 1".**

• **'Grandiosity' **is spelled correctly. The word means an **inflated sense of one's importance or stature. **It's a noun form of **'grandiose', **implying that **one's aspiration or actions **are exaggerated to the point of being pompous or pretentious.
 
• **'Conservation' **is also spelled correctly. It is the act of conserving something – for example, **preventing wastage or guarding from loss or degradation. **
 
• In the context of **'biodiversity', **it generally refers to ensuring the continued existence and variety of plant and animal life in the world.
 
• **'Align' **is spelled **properly. **Usually, the word **'align' **is used to indicate **an arrangement in a straight line or in parallel, or to position (something) in relation to something else. **
 
 
• **​**When used in relation to goals or objectives, it means to bring them into harmony or agreement.
 
 
 
• In conclusion, the correct answer is **'citizentry' **due to its incorrect spelling.
 
 
• The correctly spelled version of the word is **'citizenry'. **
 
• The sentence, when corrected, would read: **"We should align our grandiosity with conservation of biodiversity while focusing on citizenry awareness."**
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

Swathi and Raghav are________ friends.

• **Hearty friends: **The word **‘hearty’ **usually collocates with words like **'meal', 'laugh', 'welcome' **etc. to express that something is done warmly, enthusiastically, or fully. It's not commonly associated with 'friends'.
 
• **Tight friends: **The term **'tight friends' **is not generally used in standard English. It might be colloquially used in certain dialects or regions, but it's not widely accepted or understood.
 
• **Deep friends: **The term **'deep friends' **is likewise not typically used in English. **'Deep' **would usually be used with **'conversation' **or **'thought', **for example, but not with **'friends'.**
 
 
 
• Taking all of these into account, the most appropriate and conventional term to use to describe a close and intimate friendship in English would be **"bosom friends".**
 
• Hence, the sentence would be: **"Swathi and Raghav are bosom friends."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

subject: ENG
question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

My brother has sent me a message.

options.text: A message has been sent to me by my brother.
I have been sent a message to by my brother.
A message have been sent to me.
A message was sent to me by my brother.

solution:
The correct answer is **"A message has been sent to me by my brother."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• The given sentence is in Present Perfect Tense and Active Voice.
 
• The rule for changing a Present Perfect Tense from Active voice to Passive voice:
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence become the subject of the passive sentence.​
 
• Subject is "My brother" and object is "a message" in active voice.
 
• So, the subject is "a message" and object is "my brother" in passive voice.
 
• Structure__:
 __
 
• Subject + has/have + V3 + Object (Active Voice)__
 
• Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject __(Passive Voice)__
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *Disha has arranged the things. *(Active Voice)
 
• *The things have been arranged by Disha.** *(Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• Therefore, the​ correct answer is Option 1.

 

​​Correct sentence: *A message has been sent to me by my brother.*

**Passive Voice: **the subject receives the action expressed by the verb.

*Usage:* when the action is the focus, not the subject or when the doer is unknown.

**Rules of Conversion from Active to Passive Voice:**

1. Identify the subject, the verb and the object: S+V+O.

2. **Change **the **object **into **subject.**

3. Put the suitable helping verb or **auxiliary verb.**

4. Change the** verb **into **past participle** of the verb.

5. Add the preposition **"by“.**

6. Change the **subject** into **object.**

Thus, the correct sentence would be:* The flyover should be avoided.*

• As there is** no particular object **mentioned in the sentence since "**that Einstein was a genius"** is **a phrase**. So it is categorized as** 'without object in passive voice. '**
 
• The phrase **"It is said that"** translates into the active form as **"People say that".**
 
• The tense of the verb should remain** consistent** with the original sentence. Here,** "say"** is in the simple present tense, matching the original sentence's implied meaning.
 
• Format of active voice :** Subject + Main verb ( simple present tense here ) + Object**

I am sometimes puzzled by her actions.

solution:
Here the correct answer is **Her actions sometimes puzzle me.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:- 

__
 
• The above-given sentence is in the passive voice.
 
• We need to change it into active voice:- 
 
• The subject 'I' becomes the object '**me**' of the active voice.
 
• The object 'her actions' becomes the subject of the active voice.
 
• Simple present tense changes in the following manner:-
 
 
• Passive Voice - is/am/are + V3
 
• Active Voice - (do/does + V1) or (V1 s/es)
 
 
 
• Thus,** 'am sometimes puzzled' **will be converted to** 'sometimes puzzle'.**

*Therefore, the correct active voice is Her actions sometimes puzzle me.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When we convert active voice to passive voice, three things need to be kept in mind:-

 
 
• Change object into subject.
 
• Change subject into object.
 
• Always use the third form of the verb in passive voice.
 
• Use 'by' before the new object.
